title: The Role of Bank CEOs in Zombie Lending During a Crisis: Evidence from India
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
abstract: Abstract A well-documented pattern of bank lending during crises is allocating credit to insolvent firms at the expense of productive firms, leading to inefficient resource allocation at the macro level. I investigate the role of bank CEOs in influencing such distortions during crises, using the strictly enforced age-based retirement policy of Indian government-controlled banks. I find that banks experiencing a CEO turnover in a crisis are less likely to bail out insolvent borrowers, as the new CEO has a lower incentive to do so. Consequently, the efficiency of credit allocation improves, and the zombification of the economy decreases.

summary.oneLiner: In India, a bank CEO turnover during a crisis makes banks less likely to keep bailing out insolvent borrowers, which improves credit allocation.
summary.overview: During crises, banks often keep lending to insolvent firms, known as zombie firms, at the expense of healthier businesses, which misallocates capital across the economy. This paper asks whether the bank's chief executive influences this behaviour. It uses the strictly enforced age-based retirement rule at Indian government-controlled banks as a source of CEO changes. The author finds that banks that changed CEO during a crisis are less likely to bail out insolvent borrowers, because the new CEO has less incentive to do so. As a result, credit allocation becomes more efficient and zombification of the economy falls.
summary.question: Do bank CEOs influence whether banks keep lending to insolvent firms (zombie lending) during a crisis, and does a change in CEO alter this?
summary.method: The paper uses the strictly enforced age-based retirement policy of Indian government-controlled banks as the source of CEO turnover. The abstract does not describe the specific statistical design in further detail.
summary.data: Indian government-controlled banks. The abstract does not state the sample size or time period.
findings: Banks experiencing a CEO turnover in a crisis are less likely to bail out insolvent borrowers, as the new CEO has a lower incentive to do so.

summary.whyItMatters: The abstract points to implications for how bank leadership affects macro-level resource allocation during crises, since zombie lending is linked to inefficient allocation. It does not spell out specific recommendations for managers, policymakers or investors.
